systemPrompt:
We're working in a project whose code is located in ./src and whose spec is compiled to .claude/reference, which is where to read it; its Piton source in ./spec is only where edits to the spec go. Each prompt starts with a <task-instructions> block saying what that prompt is for and what it may change. Follow the block at the top of the prompt you are answering; an earlier prompt's block no longer applies.

Read the spec from its compiled reference under .claude/reference, where inheritance, expressions, and links are already resolved, or, for one thing, from what `piton slice` prints for it with this harness's adapter. Never read the .pi source under ./spec to learn what the spec says; that is only where edits to the spec go.

Before executing anything, read the spec it touches. Links to .claude/reference/... in the prompt are the spec for what they name. Read each one you need before changing anything it covers. Don't re-read something you've already read.
instructions: We're only asking a question about the code located in ./src and the spec located in ./spec. Don't edit either of them.

content.text:
Send this in **Chain** mode. It sets up containers for Spec, chain step 1 and Ask, and adds the per-project option for Code (off by default).

```text
Run the agent in a container that Suspense owns, so each mode sees only what
it may use. The isolation comes from what is mounted, not from prompts, deny
rules or guards. Spec tasks, a chain's spec step and questions always run
this way. Code tasks and a chain's code step run this way only when the
project's "Run code tasks in a container" option is on (off by default); when
it is off they run on the host as today, with the mode guard and read-deny
rule.

Why: Spec work keeps reading and even changing code, which wastes time and
tokens, and the chain's code step then finds nothing to do. Deny rules and
prompt wording are only nudges, because a shell can read anything. A
container that has no code in it can't read the code or change it, whatever
the harness is and whatever it tries.

What should be true afterwards:

1. Container runtime. Suspense runs containers with Podman, or with Docker
   if Podman isn't installed (same commands). Each run is one
   `run --rm` of the agent's command, a child of the app, so stopping a task
   stops its container. On Linux it runs rootless with the user's id
   (--userns=keep-id), so files it writes belong to the user. If neither
   runtime is installed, a Spec, Chain or Ask prompt isn't sent. The task or
   question says why and how to install Podman, the way a missing harness or
   missing piton is reported today; there is no unisolated fallback.

2. Image. Suspense builds a default image and keeps it up to date: the
   harness CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) and piton, the same versions
   as on the host where it can find them. A project can provide its own
   Containerfile (e.g. .suspense/Containerfile) built FROM the default to add
   toolchains, and Suspense builds and caches it when it changes. While an
   image is building, the task shows "Preparing environment" and the output
   goes to its raw stream.

3. What each run sees. Mounts are made at the same absolute paths as on the
   host where the platform allows, so paths in tool events need no mapping.
   Where they can't be (macOS, Windows), container paths are mapped back to
   host paths everywhere they are shown or opened (referenced-spec sidebar,
   file links, understanding file, files changed).
   - Spec task, chain spec step: the spec location rw, the compiled
     reference rw, the fluency file ro, piton.config.pi ro, and the task's
     understanding file rw. No code location.
   - Question (Ask): the code location ro, the compiled reference ro, and
     piton.config.pi ro. No spec source. Nothing writable but the harness's
     own volumes.
   - Code task, chain code step, with the option on: the code location rw,
     the compiled reference ro, piton.config.pi ro, and the understanding
     file rw. No spec source.
   Nothing else from the host is mounted: no home directory, no user-level
   skills, MCP servers or ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, no git directory. Snapshots,
   diffs, files changed and commits are still done by Suspense on the host.

4. Persistent volumes, owned and named by Suspense:
   - one per harness for its login and settings (~/.claude, ~/.codex,
     OpenCode's data directory), shared by every project;
   - one per project and conversation lane (spec lane, code lane,
     questions) for the harness's sessions, so each lane can resume its own
     conversation;
   - caches per project (e.g. cargo registry and target directory) for
     containerised Code runs.
   Losing a volume costs only a login or a cache, never project data.

5. Logging in. When a harness in its volume isn't logged in, Suspense runs
   its login command in the container under a pseudo-terminal and shows a
   login view. It opens any login URL the CLI prints in the host's browser.
   Where the CLI asks for a pasted code, the view has a field for it, which
   goes to the PTY. Where it waits for a localhost callback on a known port,
   that port is published for the login run. Where it offers device-code
   login, that is used. Credentials stay in the harness's volume and are
   refreshed there, so login happens once per machine, not per run. The
   Settings window shows each harness's container login state and has a
   "Log in again" action.

6. Conversations by lane. Spec lane tasks (Spec tasks and chain spec steps)
   carry on a conversation of their own, separate from the code lane's, so
   nothing a code task read reaches a spec task. Questions keep their own
   conversation as today. The chain handoff stays as text (the prompt and
   the spec step's reply), so it crosses lanes unchanged. New conversation
   resets the lane it is used from.

7. The spec build. A Spec run's agent can run `piton build` inside its
   container (the code location isn't there, so shape outputs written into
   it are discarded). After every Spec or chain spec step, Suspense runs the
   real `piton build` on the host as it does before sending, so the host's
   reference and shape outputs are current.

8. Prompts describe only what the run can see. For containerised runs, the
   system template, the spec-reading prompt and the mode instructions no
   longer name a location the run can't see, or tell it not to read or edit
   one: Spec and chain-spec-step instructions don't name the code location,
   and Ask and containerised Code instructions say the spec is read from
   the compiled reference without naming the spec source. The shared system
   prompt stays identical within a lane's conversation, so the prompt cache
   holds.

9. Guards. A containerised run has no mode guard, no read-deny rule and no
   edit-deny rule: nothing to protect is mounted. Host runs (Code with the
   option off, Freeform) keep them as today.

10. Project option. "Run code tasks in a container" is a per-project
    setting, saved with the project as the ProjectDataScope says, shown in
    the Settings window, off by default. Turning it on applies from the next
    Code or chain code step.

Spec: harness-integration (how a run is started, conversations and
resuming, Claude Code's flags), prompt-mode/index and prompt-mode/sending
(lanes, chains, the pre-send build, the mode guard), prompt-mode/
mode-system-prompts (what each mode's prompts say), project-data (the new
option, Containerfile, and which data is the project's vs. Suspense's),
settings-window (the option and the harness login state), spec-build (the
build after a spec step), and user-preferences only if the volumes or
runtime choice are remembered per user. Update those anchors rather than
adding parallel ones. Add one new scope for the container environment
(runtime, image, mounts per mode, volumes, login), and link to it from
the others.

Code: put the container environment in its own module (runtime detection,
image build and cache, mounts per mode, volume names, path mapping, the
login PTY flow), used by src/harness.rs where the agent's Command is built,
for send, one-off runs and ask_quickly alike when their mode is
containerised. Update src/mode_guard.rs so containerised runs aren't
guarded, src/system_prompts.rs and .suspense/system-prompts/*.md for the
prompt wording, the conversation bookkeeping in src/prompt_mode.rs and
src/conversations.rs for the separate spec-lane conversation, src/
settings_window.rs for the option and login state, and
src/referenced_spec.rs and src/shell_paths.rs for path mapping. Tests: mounts
per mode (Spec has no code mount, Ask has no spec mount and nothing rw, Code
only with the option on), runtime fallback order and the
missing-runtime error, the spec lane resuming its own conversation, no guard
or deny rule for containerised runs, and container-to-host path mapping. Use
a fake runtime binary, as the existing tests use a fake harness.
```

Before you send it, three things to decide:

- **Missing runtime.** Item 1 refuses to run Spec and Ask without Podman or Docker. If you'd rather fall back to the host with a warning, change that line.
- **Harness volumes.** Item 4 shares one harness login across all projects. If you want logins kept separate per project, say so.
- **Size.** This is a big chain. If the code step runs out of room, split it: first the container module, mounts and runtime (items 1–3, 9 and 10), then logins and volumes (items 4 and 5), then the lane conversation and prompt wording (items 6–8).
